name: Paradev
description: Paradev (formerly Superset) is an agentic IDE to orchestrate 100+ coding agents in parallel. Run any agent with your own subscription.
readmeExcerpt:
### Paradev Run Claude Code, Codex, or another CLI agent with terminals, code review, and browser previews in one workspace. [**Download for macOS**](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest)  •  [Documentation](https://docs.paradev.com)  •  [Changelog](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases)  •  [Discord](https://discord.gg/cZeD9WYcV7)

### Documentation for agents The docs are available as [a Markdown index](https://docs.paradev.com/llms.txt) linking to individual pages, or [one full-text file](https://docs.paradev.com/llms-full.txt). ## Install Download the desktop app: - **macOS**: [Apple Silicon (.dmg)](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest/download/Superset-arm64.dmg) · [Intel (.dmg)](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest/download/Superset-x64.dmg) - **Linux**: [x64 AppImage](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest/download/Superset-x86_64.AppImage) (experimental; macOS is the primary target) - **Windows**: not yet available - [All builds](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest) All you need installed is [Git](https://git-scm.com/). [gh](https://cli.github.com/) is optional and enables the PR workflows; Paradev offers to install it for you. ## Start with one task 1. [Install Paradev](#install) and add a repository from your computer or clone one. 2. Create a workspace, choose your CLI agent, and describe a small change you want to make. 3. Inspect its patch in **Changes**, run the relevant tests, and preview your app in the browser pane before committing. For a walkthrough of workspace creation and review, see [Your First Parallel Session](https://docs.paradev.com/first-workspace). ## Review and revise - **Change your app's UI.** Use **Design** in the browser pane to select an element and send your requested change to an agent with element context. [Walkthrough](https://paradev.com/blog/change-ui-with-your-coding-agent) · [Design Mode docs](https://docs.paradev.com/browser#design-mode) - **Ask an agent to fix a PR.** Open **Pull requests → Code**, select diff lines, and send feedback to a running or new agent session. Posting to GitHub is optional. [Walkthrough](https://paradev.com/blog/send-pr-feedback-to-your-agent) · [PR docs](https://docs.paradev.com/pull-requests#comment-straight-to-an-agent) - **Review a report with your team.** Ask an agent to publish a Page. Teammates pin comments, and a watching agent can revise it at the same link. Keep its host and session running for feedback delivery. [Walkthrough](https://paradev.com/blog/review-agent-work-with-pages) · [Pages docs](https://docs.paradev.com/pages)
See the diff viewer and browser previews ### Built-in Diff Viewer Inspect, comment on, and edit agent changes without leaving the app, then commit and push when it's ready. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/diff-viewer) ### In-App Browser & Ports Preview running dev servers in a browser pane. Ports are detected per workspace, so every worktree gets its own preview. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/browser)
## Run independent tasks Give each task a Git worktree with its own branch and terminals. Worktrees separate working files; they do not sandbox processes or prevent merge conflicts. [Workspace docs](https://docs.paradev.com/workspaces) · [Terminal docs](https://docs.paradev.com/terminal-integration) · [Agent status](https://docs.paradev.com/agent-integration)
See workspaces, monitoring, terminals, and the command palette ### Parallel Workspaces Review each result before merging, or try two approaches to the same problem and keep the one you prefer. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/workspaces) ### Agent Monitoring Track every agent from the sidebar, with working indicators, completion chimes, and dock badges when one needs your attention. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/agent-integration) ### Built-in Terminal Tabs, infinite splits, presets, and persistent sessions that survive restarts. Press ⌘I for a rich prompt editor with multiline editing and @-file mentions. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/terminal-integration) ### Command Palette Jump to any workspace, action, or setting from one search box. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/keyboard-shortcuts)
## Work across devices and on a schedule Connect another machine to reach its workspaces remotely, or schedule an agent to work on a recurring task. The CLI, SDK, and MCP server also let agents and scripts manage workspaces. Mobile supports **iPhone and iPad** and requires **Paradev Pro** and **iOS 26 or iPadOS 26 or later**. Use cloud workspaces without keeping your own computer connected. To reach workspaces on your own computer, enable **Remote Access** and keep that host awake and online. [Remote access](https://docs.paradev.com/remote-access) · [Automations](https://docs.paradev.com/automations) · [iPhone and iPad](https://paradev.com/mobile) · [CLI](https://docs.paradev.com/cli/getting-started)
See mobile, automations, remote access, and the CLI ### Paradev for iPhone and iPad Control Claude Code, Codex, and other terminal agents in cloud workspaces or on your connected computer. Pick up the same workspaces and terminal sessions, send follow-up prompts, review diffs, and merge PRs from your iPhone or iPad. [**Download on the App Store**](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6788926383)  •  [Learn more →](https://paradev.com/mobile) ### Automations Run agent sessions on a schedule or when something happens: review a PR when you're asked, triage a new Sentry issue, pick up a bug report from Slack, draft the weekly changelog. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/automations) ### Remote Access Connect another machine and reach its workspaces from anywhere: the desktop app, the CLI, or your phone. Wake offline hosts with a custom command. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/remote-access) ### Paradev CLI Script it from any shell: create workspaces, launch agents, read their terminals, and manage automations with a single binary. If an agent can run a command, it can drive Paradev. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/cli/getting-started)
## Customize your workflow - **[Built-in skills](https://docs.paradev.com/skills)**: agents come pre-loaded with `superset:*` skills (orchestrate parallel agents, schedule automations, file feedback, diagnose issues), provisioned automatically at launch - **[Workspace setup scripts](https://docs.paradev.com/setup-teardown-scripts)**: automate env setup, dependency installs, and dev servers per workspace - **[Terminal presets](https://docs.paradev.com/terminal-presets)**: save agent and shell layouts and open them with one keystroke - **[Slack & Linear](https://docs.paradev.com/use-with-linear)**: spin up workspaces from Slack messages or Linear issues - **[Open in your IDE](https://docs.paradev.com/use-with-ide)**: one-click handoff to Cursor, VS Code, or any editor - **[Custom themes](https://docs.paradev.com/custom-themes)**: build, edit, and import theme files - **[Keyboard shortcuts](https://docs.paradev.com/keyboard-shortcuts)**: every action is remappable via **Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts** (⌘/) - **[Bring your own providers](https://docs.paradev.com/providers)**: connect OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex, or Vercel AI Gateway - **And many more**: we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The [changelog](https://paradev.com/changelog) is the real feature list. ## Supported Agents Keep your existing agent subscriptions. Use Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, or another CLI coding agent.
Browse supported agents | Agent | Status | |:------|:-------| |  [Amp Code](https://ampcode.com/) | Fully supported | |  [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/) | Fully supported | |  [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) | Fully supported | |  [OpenAI Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) | Fully supported | |  [Cursor Agent](https://docs.cursor.com/agent) | Fully supported | |  [Droid](https://www.factory.ai/) | Fully supported | |  [fx](https://fx.sh/) | Fully supported | |  [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/goo

Paradev

Run Claude Code, Codex, or another CLI agent with terminals, code review, and browser previews in one workspace.

Download for macOS  •  Documentation  •  Changelog  •  Discord

Documentation for agents

The docs are available as a Markdown index linking to individual pages, or one full-text file.

Install

Download the desktop app:

  • macOS: Apple Silicon (.dmg) · Intel (.dmg)
  • Linux: x64 AppImage (experimental; macOS is the primary target)
  • Windows: not yet available
  • All builds

All you need installed is Git. gh is optional and enables the PR workflows; Paradev offers to install it for you.

Start with one task

  1. Install Paradev and add a repository from your computer or clone one.
  2. Create a workspace, choose your CLI agent, and describe a small change you want to make.
  3. Inspect its patch in Changes, run the relevant tests, and preview your app in the browser pane before committing.

For a walkthrough of workspace creation and review, see Your First Parallel Session.

Review and revise

  • Change your app's UI. Use Design in the browser pane to select an element and send your requested change to an agent with element context. Walkthrough · Design Mode docs
  • Ask an agent to fix a PR. Open Pull requests → Code, select diff lines, and send feedback to a running or new agent session. Posting to GitHub is optional. Walkthrough · PR docs
  • Review a report with your team. Ask an agent to publish a Page. Teammates pin comments, and a watching agent can revise it at the same link. Keep its host and session running for feedback delivery. Walkthrough · Pages docs
See the diff viewer and browser previews

Inspect, comment on, and edit agent changes without leaving the app, then commit and push when it's ready.

Docs →

Preview running dev servers in a browser pane. Ports are detected per workspace, so every worktree gets its own preview.

Docs →

Docs →

Jump to any workspace, action, or setting from one search box.

Docs →

Work across devices and on a schedule

Connect another machine to reach its workspaces remotely, or schedule an agent to work on a recurring task. The CLI, SDK, and MCP server also let agents and scripts manage workspaces.

Mobile supports iPhone and iPad and requires Paradev Pro and iOS 26 or iPadOS 26 or later. Use cloud workspaces without keeping your own computer connected. To reach workspaces on your own computer, enable Remote Access and keep that host awake and online.

Remote access · Automations · iPhone and iPad · CLI

See mobile, automations, remote access, and the CLI

Paradev for iPhone and iPad

Control Claude Code, Codex, and other terminal agents in cloud workspaces or on your connected computer. Pick up the same workspaces and terminal sessions, send follow-up prompts, review diffs, and merge PRs from your iPhone or iPad.

Download on the App Store  •  Learn more →

Automations

Run agent sessions on a schedule or when something happens: review a PR when you're asked, triage a new Sentry issue, pick up a bug report from Slack, draft the weekly changelog.

Docs →

Remote Access

Connect another machine and reach its workspaces from anywhere: the desktop app, the CLI, or your phone. Wake offline hosts with a custom command.

Docs →

Paradev CLI

Script it from any shell: create workspaces, launch agents, read their terminals, and manage automations with a single binary. If an agent can run a command, it can drive Paradev.

Docs →

Customize your workflow

  • Built-in skills: agents come pre-loaded with superset:* skills (orchestrate parallel agents, schedule automations, file feedback, diagnose issues), provisioned automatically at launch
  • Workspace setup scripts: automate env setup, dependency installs, and dev servers per workspace
  • Terminal presets: save agent and shell layouts and open them with one keystroke
  • Slack & Linear: spin up workspaces from Slack messages or Linear issues
  • Open in your IDE: one-click handoff to Cursor, VS Code, or any editor
  • Custom themes: build, edit, and import theme files
  • Keyboard shortcuts: every action is remappable via Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts (⌘/)
  • Bring your own providers: connect OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex, or Vercel AI Gateway
  • And many more: we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The changelog is the real feature list.

Supported Agents

Keep your existing agent subscriptions.

Use Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, or another CLI coding agent.

Browse supported agents
Agent Status
 Amp Code Fully supported
 Antigravity CLI Fully supported
 Claude Code Fully supported
 OpenAI Codex CLI Fully supported
 Cursor Agent Fully supported
 Droid Fully supported
 fx Fully supported
 Gemini CLI Fully supported
 GitHub Copilot Fully supported
 Grok Fully supported
 Hermes Fully supported
 Muse Code Fully supported
 Devin Fully supported
 Kimi Code Fully supported
 Kiro Fully supported
 Mastra Code Fully supported
 Mistral Vibe Fully supported
 Oh My Pi Fully supported
 OpenCode Fully supported
 Pi Fully supported
 Polygraph Fully supported
Any other CLI agent Works without configuration

Agents get more than a terminal:

  • Model picker: choose a model and reasoning effort when you launch an agent
  • Per-agent settings: tune launch commands, prompt templates, and model overrides in Settings → Agents
  • Custom agents: add any terminal agent with its own icon and it works like a built-in
  • Built-in chat: talk to models in a chat pane, with inline tool approvals and plan review

More Than a Desktop App

Every surface talks to the same workspaces, so you can start a task in the app and check on it from anywhere.

Surface What you get
Desktop App The full IDE: terminals, diff viewer, in-app browser, automations
CLI A single superset binary to manage workspaces, agents, terminals, and hosts from any shell
TypeScript SDK Drive Paradev programmatically with @superset_sh/sdk from Node, Bun, or Deno
MCP Server Let Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other agents create and manage workspaces themselves

The CLI comes bundled with the desktop app, or install it standalone:

curl -fsSL https://paradev.com/cli/install.sh | sh
# or
brew install paradevai/tap/superset

Development

Want to hack on Paradev or contribute a PR? Clone the repository, add it to the installed Paradev app, and create a workspace for your change:

git clone https://github.com/paradevai/paradev.git

Then run the development setup from that workspace terminal:

./.superset/setup.local.sh
bun run dev

Run setup.local.sh once in every new worktree. It configures workspace-specific app identity and ports so the development desktop app can run alongside the installed Paradev app and other development worktrees.

No Neon account or third-party credentials are needed. setup.local.sh brings up a local Postgres + neon-proxy + Redis stack via Docker and seeds a dev account. Sign in with the "Sign in as dev" button (or admin@local.test / supersetdev).

Prereqs for building from source (to use Paradev, install the app instead): Bun v1.4.3+ (pinned in .bun-version), docker, jq, and gh (brew install jq gh).

See DEVELOPMENT.md for the full guide: what the setup script does, manual setup against real services, common commands, troubleshooting, and how to build the desktop app. Contribution process lives in CONTRIBUTING.md.

Configuration

Configure workspace setup, teardown, and run scripts in .superset/config.json. See full documentation.

{
  "setup": ["./.superset/setup.sh"],
  "teardown": ["./.superset/teardown.sh"],
  "run": ["./.superset/run.sh"]
}

Tech Stack

Browse the implementation stack

Private by Default

  • Explicit Connections: you choose which agents, providers, and integrations to connect.

Contributing

We welcome contributions! See CONTRIBUTING.md for how to get set up and open a PR. Bugs and feature requests go in issues.

🌐 Read this in other languages

English | 日本語 | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 한국어 | Français | Español | Deutsch | Português | Italiano | Русский | Türkçe | Polski | Nederlands | Bahasa Indonesia | Čeština | Tiếng Việt

Community

Join the Paradev community to get help, share feedback, and connect with other users:

  • Discord: chat with the team and community
  • Twitter: follow for updates and announcements
  • GitHub Issues: report bugs and request features
  • GitHub Discussions: ask questions and share ideas

Team

License & what's free forever

The desktop app is free forever. Running agents in parallel on your own machine will never require payment. Anything we charge for will be an optional service on top.

The whole app is in this repo under the Elastic License 2.0: use it, fork it, modify it, self-host it for your team. The only thing off the table is repackaging Paradev itself as a service you sell to others.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A cross-platform desktop IDE for discovering, configuring, and orchestrating multiple AI CLI agents simultaneously.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Superset is a desktop application built to serve as a unified control center for AI coding agents. Rather than running agents in disconnected terminal windows, Superset provides a graphical interface to discover, connect, and manage various AI systems side-by-side in isolated git worktrees. It runs agents locally without context switching overhead, giving each its own terminal and environment. The application includes built-in diff viewers, automated scheduling, and remote host connections to securely orchestrate complex agent workflows across different machines. By orchestrating Claude Code, Codex, and other agents in parallel, it significantly reduces manual waiting periods.
keyFeatures: Parallel Workspaces: Orchestrate and monitor over 100 CLI agents at once, each isolated in its own git worktree.
Built-in Terminal: Features tabs, infinite splits, and a rich prompt editor with multiline editing and file mentions.
Integrated Diff Viewer: Inspect, comment on, and edit agent changes directly within the application before committing.
In-App Browser Previews: View running dev servers with automatic port detection isolated to each specific worktree.
Scheduled Automations: Run agent sessions automatically overnight to triage issues, update dependencies, or draft changelogs.
Terminal Workflows: Includes tabs, splits, and multiline editing directly within the isolated environment.

useCases.title: Rapid Iteration
useCases.description: Engineers deploy concurrent agents across branches to test multiple solutions simultaneously.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers and AI practitioners who need a unified, graphical IDE to manage complex, multi-agent coding workflows locally or remotely. It enables data visualization and exploration.
